maya: Heads-up — during canary bring-up for razor-2-int8 we're seeing a spike in structured-output (funcall) parse failures. Canary vs baseline: parse_failure_rate ~3.2% vs baseline 0.3%.

maya: Symptoms: broken JSON objects with extraneous tokens prefixed from the KV cache when requests are batched/streamed. Only shows up when `kv_merge=true` and `streaming=true` on int8 canary.

ron: Interesting. Any examples of the corrupted output?

maya: Yep pasted a raw snippet I pulled from the canary logs: 
```
...prefix tokens... }}][{\n{"action":"create","tool":"db","args":{"id":123}}\n```
So you get trailing `}}][{` before the JSON. Parser bails.

luke: That looks like two concatenated prefix fragments. Could be kv-cache collision on the batch boundary — if two requests share a prefix buffer and streaming flush interleaves.

jen: Is this only on int8? Any evidence quantization changed tokenization/kernel ordering?

maya: We only see it on the int8 canary so far. Baseline fp16 doesn't show it. Sequence-level token logs show odd token IDs (reserved control tokens) getting emitted right before the `{`.

qa-bot: Quick stats from the canary run (10k prompts): total_funcall=10,000, parse_fail=322, truncated=14, unparsable_noise=308. Failing prompts concentrated in batch sizes >=4 and with kv_prefix_length>128.

ron: Two quick experiments to try: (1) disable streaming on canary but keep int8 to see if it's stream-flush related; (2) reduce batch size to 1-2 to check if batching merges are the cause.

maya: I ran (1) — disabling streaming dropped parse failures to 0.7% (so big reduction).

luke: That strongly implicates stream/flush path. Maybe an ordering bug in the int8 kernel where partial KV fragments get emitted into the stream buffer without delimiter.

jen: Any recent kernel changes? I remember a PR around microquant kernel's output buffer pooling last week. @ron did your team touch stream flush code?

ron: We did a minor refactor: `streamer->emit_chunk` now uses `memcpy` into a ring buffer that assumes contiguous chunks; could be a race when KV merge writes while a different request is flushing. Reverting that would be quick to test.

ops-bot: Deploy note: rolled canary to cluster-a on 2026-06-20T14:12Z with tag razor-2-int8-canary-20260620.

maya: Proposed mitigations while we root-cause:
- Add in-service `json_guard` that scans stream for first `{` and last `}` and extracts JSON block before parse (best-effort repair).
- Force a deterministic separator token before function/toolcall generations (e.g., `\n---JSON_START---\n`).
- Short-term: disable streaming for tool-calls on int8 models.

jen: json_guard helps but it's a heuristic. We should track rescued vs original parse to alert if rescue rate grows. Add telemetry: `rescue_rate` + `rescue_aggressiveness` tag.

luke: Also add a micro-eval: run 5k prompts with `kv_merge=false` and `streaming=true` to see if kv_merge specifically is needed for the bug.

maya: Plan for next 48h:
- Ron to revert ring-buffer refactor on a canary build and run 5k streaming canary tests.
- Luke to run kv_merge=false micro-eval across 2 seeds (5k each).
- Jen/QA to add json_guard and telemetry to canary proxy and run a 10k sample to measure rescue_rate.

ron: On it. I'll post build id and logs here. If reverting removes the noise we can ship a proper fix for the ring buffer + a unit test to assert chunk boundaries.

qa-bot: Noted. Adding an alert: if parse_failure_rate > 1% for 1h on any dedicated region, page oncall.

maya: Thanks. One more note: some of the failing prompts are sensitive to tokenization around anonymized user IDs — might be edge-case where quantized kernels emit an extra sentinel. I'll attach a small corpus of 200 failing prompts to the canary run PR for model team.

luke: Good. Also consider adding a downstream parser tolerant mode that retries parse after sweeping for ascii noise and reparse; cheap and buys time.

jen: Agree. Let's avoid long-term heuristics that mask kernel issues. Short-term guard + telemetry + revert-fix seems right.

maya: I'll update the canary ticket with the experiment checklist and ETA tomorrow. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ron: FYI build posted: razor-2-int8-canary-20260620-rc2 — running 5k now, will drop logs at /s3/canaries/razor2/rc2/logs.

ops-bot: Test run completed: 5k streaming requests rc2. parse_failure_rate=0.4% (down from 3.2%).

maya: Promising. Keep monitoring.

jen: If rc2 holds, let's stage a patched canary across both regions and schedule a postmortem doc after final fix.

maya: Closing thread for now — will reopen if new spikes appear.
